$comment: Which samples in samples/workflows/ become recipe pages under docs/recipes/. `pnpm --filter @ai-orchestrator/docs gen:recipes` (run by the docs build and dev server) writes them. Fields: sample (file name); slug (page name; never rename a published slug, GitHub Pages cannot redirect); title (<= 54 characters, the page title adds ' | L2M'); description (<= 155 characters); keys (none | model | services: what it needs to run); keysNote (one short line, e.g. 'No API key'); time (optional, e.g. '5 minutes'); tags (lower case, the filters on /recipes/); whatYouGet (one sentence); summary (Markdown paragraph: what it does and when to use it); makeItYours and makeItSafer (Markdown lists, optional; safety controls are optional features, say so); related (glossary slugs); docs (further reading inside the docs).

recipes.title: Build an MCP agent with no API key in 5 minutes
recipes.description: Import a ready MCP agent that runs on a fresh L2M install with a built-in echo model and a mock MCP server, then swap in a real model and server.
recipes.whatYouGet: One agent with a chat model and two MCP tools, a clock and a calculator, that runs on a fresh install.
recipes.summary: A manual trigger starts one Agent Orchestrator node, which can call two tools from the bundled mock MCP server: `get_current_time` and `calculator`. The chat model is the built-in echo provider, so the workflow imports and runs with no key. Echo is not a real model: it never asks for a tool, so a local run ends after one model call. The demo's recorded run of this workflow shows the same single call. To watch the full loop with tool calls, open the [support agent in the live demo](https://lsquarem.com/demo/?mode=editor&workflowId=wf-demo-support-agent&demoRun=recorded), recorded with a scripted stand-in model, or attach a real chat model.
recipes.makeItYours:
- Replace the echo chat model node with a real one (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) on the agent's `chat_model` port.
- Replace the mock MCP tools with a server from your [MCP server registry](/product/mcp-server-registry), such as a filesystem or database server.
- Write your own system prompt on the agent node, and raise `maxIterations` only if the task needs more steps.
recipes.makeItSafer:
- Deny or allow tools per role with [MCP tool policy](/product/mcp-tool-policy).
- Require a person's approval before write tools run: see [human approval for agent tool calls](/guides/human-approval-for-agent-tool-calls).
- Cap model spend with a [budget](/product/budgets).

recipes.title: Supervisor and worker agents: a runnable example
recipes.description: A supervisor agent hands work to a researcher and a calculator worker, each with its own tools. Imports and runs with no API key.
recipes.whatYouGet: A Supervisor agent with two worker agents, each with its own chat model and MCP tools, that runs on a fresh install.
recipes.summary: A Supervisor node coordinates two worker agents. The researcher has an MCP knowledge-base lookup tool; the computer has a calculator and a clock. The Supervisor sees each worker as one tool and decides which to call for each step, and each worker runs its own agent loop. Every agent uses the built-in echo provider and the bundled mock MCP server, so it runs with no API key. Echo never asks for a tool, so the Supervisor answers on its first turn and hands nothing off; attach a real chat model to see it delegate.
recipes.makeItYours:
- Give each worker its own real chat model on its `chat_model` port: a small, cheap model often does for a narrow worker.
- Swap a worker's mock tools for your own MCP servers.
- Add a third worker on the Supervisor's `worker` port when a new kind of task appears, rather than giving one agent every tool.
recipes.makeItSafer:
- Keep write tools on one worker only, and require approval for them: see [human approval for agent tool calls](/guides/human-approval-for-agent-tool-calls).
- Record a good run as a [golden run](/product/golden-runs) and replay it after each change.
